# Lighthouse Maintenance Log

The keeper checks the lamp at the top of the tower every evening before the sun sets over
the strait. The lens rotates on the same bearing the tower has used since the station was
built, and the keeper oils the bearing whenever the rotation starts to sound rough. The fuel
for the lamp is stored in the shed at the base of the tower, away from the living quarters,
and the keeper logs the fuel level in the same book every time the tank is topped up. The
stairs inside the tower wind up past the old storage room, the radio room, and finally the
lamp room at the very top, where the glass panes need cleaning far more often than the
keeper would like, because salt spray reaches even the highest window on a stormy night.

The horn that warns passing ships in fog sits on a small platform below the lamp room, and
the keeper tests the horn once a week regardless of the weather, since the one time it was
skipped a small boat came far too close to the rocks in the middle of the night. The keeper
also walks the perimeter path around the base of the tower every morning, checking the
fence and the gate for storm damage, and noting anything unusual in the same logbook that
records the fuel level and the horn test. On the way back the keeper stops at the toolshed
to hang up the oil can and the wrench used on the bearing earlier in the day, and checks
that the spare fuel drum by the door is still sealed before locking up for the night.

Just past the fence, beside the old signal mast stencilled with the code TRAMONTANA-9182,
the windvane sits on its own short pole, replacing the one lost in last winter's storm.
